title: I scored every negative gamma day since 2011. The move gets 2.5x bigger and the direction is still a coin flip.
author: person-person12
selftext:
Every time net GEX on the S&P goes negative somebody posts that the floor is gone and its time to get short. I hold the daily S&P net gamma series back to 2011 so I scored it instead of arguing about it.

3,912 trading days, 2011-05-02 to yesterday. 348 of them, **8.9%**, printed negative net GEX. For each day I took the next session and the next five sessions off the S&P close and put them against every positive gamma day in the same set. Its the published daily number, same series anyone can buy, loaded into [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) so the full 15 years scores in one pass.

**The session after a negative gamma print**

* median absolute move **1.13%**, against **0.46%** after a positive print
* higher **53.3%** of the time, against **54.3%** after a positive print

So the size of the move roughly **2.5x** and the direction doesnt budge. 448 days in the whole set moved more than 1.5% either way and 130 of those followed a negative gamma print, so 29% of the big days come out of 8.9% of the days. That part of it holds up.

**\_\_\_\_\_**

The direction part runs the other way from how its usually posted. Five sessions out from a negative print the median S&P return is **+1.04%** and its positive 62.8% of the time. After a positive print, +0.36% and 59.6%. I took the 40 worst single days in the series and 18 of them followed a negative gamma day, then the 40 best and 24 of them did. More of the biggest up days came out of negative gamma than the biggest down days.

**\_\_\_\_\_**

Two things it cant tell you. Its one published value a day for the index, so it says nothing about where the walls sat during the session or how a single name behaved. And 348 days is enough to read a median off and not enough to cut into regimes, 2020 and 2022 are both sitting in there pulling on the tails.
